title: "Expanded evidence extraction: preoperative pathology evaluation in prolapse"
format:
  docx:
    toc: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

This extraction supports preliminary model calibration; it is not a
procedure-specific comparative effectiveness estimate. The target population
is asymptomatic postmenopausal women with stage III uterovaginal prolapse.
Published mixed-population studies are labeled as indirect.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-expanded-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Source-level evidence, including numerator/denominator and applicability"
source_rows <- readr::read_csv(
  "evidence/expanded_screening_extraction_20261109.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
display_rows <- source_rows |>
  dplyr::filter(evidence_class != "missing") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Count = dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(numerator) & !is.na(denominator),
      paste0(numerator, "/", denominator),
      "—"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    procedure_group, parameter, Count, published_estimate,
    evidence_class, limitations
  )
knitr::kable(display_rows)
```

## Highest-priority unobserved parameters

```{r}
#| label: tbl-critical-gaps
#| tbl-cap: "Missing inputs for decision modeling"
source_rows |>
  dplyr::filter(evidence_class == "missing") |>
  dplyr::select(procedure_group, parameter, limitations) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Rules for using these data

- Use 1/317 for the observed EIN proportion in the asymptomatic
  postmenopausal cohort; do not substitute the 2/106 rate of *combined*
  premalignant/malignant pathology *among patients with polyps*.
- The 8/462 complex atypical hyperplasia estimate comes from a broader POP
  hysterectomy series and is not restricted to postmenopausal patients in the
  reported denominator.
- The 10/30 second-staging estimate is conditional on incidental endometrial
  cancer. Do not apply it to the general prolapse population.
- A 38% complication estimate among selected *inpatient* trachelectomies after SCH does
  not estimate the probability of complications after SCH itself.
- Future cervix surveillance needs screening eligibility, prior CIN2+/AIS,
  age, and time horizon; screening is not automatically lifelong.
- Keep incident cancer after hysteropexy separate from occult cancer present
  at the index operation; the current model only represents prevalent disease.
- Test performance borrowed from patients with postmenopausal bleeding
  should be sensitivity analyses until validated for asymptomatic patients.
- Do not infer the causal value of earlier detection from survival comparisons
  of patients whose cancer was found before versus after prolapse surgery.

## Interpretation

Current evidence can justify broad sensitivity distributions for occult
endometrial cancer and can inform conditional second-staging probabilities
following unexpected cancer. It is not sufficient to estimate the effect of
routine testing on cancer mortality, the absolute post-hysteropexy diagnostic
delay, or the absolute probability of trachelectomy after SCH.
Those missing quantities should remain explicit scenario parameters.

The source URLs and study-specific limitations are retained in the linked CSV
for audit and future manuscript references.


## SCH with mesh sacrocolpopexy: unexpected endometrial pathology

In a retrospective single-center series of 226 sacrocolpopexies with
concomitant supracervical hysterectomy, histopathology identified atypical
endometrial hyperplasia in 14/226 (6.2%) and endometrial carcinoma in 1/226
(0.4%). All 15 patients had reportedly undergone preoperative pelvic
ultrasound and cervical cytology without suspicious findings. These tests
cannot be interpreted as validated endometrial screening with negative
predictive value in asymptomatic women. The 6.2% atypia estimate is much
higher than other prolapse cohorts; it is a heterogeneity signal and **not**
a default EIN prevalence parameter. [6]

### Management observed in the case series

Two patients with focal atypia whose specimens underwent uncontained power
morcellation received progestin therapy and clinical/ultrasound surveillance,
without immediate reoperation. The 80-year-old patient with a stage I
endometrial carcinoma underwent imaging assessment and surveillance instead
of trachelectomy after individualized multidisciplinary evaluation. The
article did not report immediate trachelectomy among these cases. No
oncologic recurrence was reported over a mean 26-month follow-up among
patients with endometrial lesions. This small, selected series and limited
follow-up do **not** establish that surveillance is oncologically equivalent
to completion surgery. [6]

For decision modeling, unexpected atypia/cancer after SCH must branch into:
(i) further assessment and surveillance, (ii) medical treatment and
surveillance, and (iii) additional surgery when indicated, potentially
including trachelectomy and oncologic staging. Assign no observed
branch probabilities from this small series: the untreated and treated
subgroups are not exchangeable, and the published description does not
establish a complete management denominator for every branch. Trachelectomy
is **not automatic** after unexpected endometrial pathology; equally, its
absence in this series is **not** evidence that it is never appropriate.

Known EIN/atypical endometrial hyperplasia should be managed according
to established guidance: ACOG identifies total hysterectomy as definitive
treatment, advises against supracervical hysterectomy as treatment for EIN,
and recommends progestin with histologic surveillance when surgery is
not an option. [7] The present study concerns *unexpected* pathology after
an SCH already performed, not planned surgery for known EIN.

6. Occult endometrial pathologies diagnosed after sacrocolpopexy with
   concomitant supracervical hysterectomy for pelvic organ prolapse.
   *Frontiers in Surgery*. 2026.
   https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12907406/
7. ACOG Clinical Consensus No. 5. Management of Endometrial
   Intraepithelial Neoplasia or Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia. 2023.
   https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-consensus/articles/2023/09/management-of-endometrial-intraepithelial-neoplasia-or-atypical-endometrial-hyperplasia
